title: token-span-aligner-and-regex-fallback-proxy-for-toolcall-streaming
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: streaming tool/function-call payloads frequently break when tokenizer subtokens split anchors used by constrained decoders (CFG/regex). This PR implements a token-span aligner + a lightweight runtime proxy that translates regex constraints to anchored CFG fallbacks when token boundaries are ambiguous, and stabilizes function-call framing in the streaming path. Key goals: 1) prevent truncated or malformed toolcall JSON in stream fragments, 2) maintain OpenAI-compat framing for function calls, 3) reduce false-positive constraint violations caused by subtoken splits.

Summary of changes: implemented a tokenizer-aware span alignment component that maps constraint token indices to byte offsets across BPE/subtoken boundaries; added a regex-to-cfg fallback proxy that synthesizes conservative CFG anchors when regex constraints would otherwise be unsafe to apply during streaming; updated stream framing to buffer partial tokens at chunk edges and to attach deterministic re-emit markers for resumed segments; added unit + integration tests that run against the openai-compat layer and a small internal regression harness.

Design notes: the span aligner hooks into the tokenizer abstraction (tokenizer/aligner.go) and exposes a best-effort mapping with confidence scores; the fallback proxy lives under constraints/proxy and is pluggable (env-controlled) so Dedicated/Private customers can opt-in to the old strict-regex behavior. A new configuration flag (constraints.streaming_mode = "safe-fallback") controls the behavior: SAFE => prefer CFG fallback on low-confidence spans, STRICT => apply regex only if full-token match.

Checklist: - [x] tokenizer span mapping implementation and comments - [x] regex->CFG fallback translator with conservative anchor generation - [x] streaming buffer/edge re-emit markers - [x] OpenAI-compat function-call framing fixes and tests - [x] e2e regression test reproducing earlier SUP-1287 incident - [x] changelog entry and migration notes - [x] performance microbenchmarks (no >3% median latency impact in our bench)

Testing: local unit test suite covers 98% of new code; integration tests run in CI with both small (gpt-lite) and medium (gpt-medium) models; added a new regression file under eval-harness/regressions/toolcall-span-split.json that reproduces the previously flaky case. CI run: build -> unit -> integration -> fuzz (only for constraint proxy). The CI pipeline initially flagged a flaky fuzz worker (seed 2143) which was addressed by tightening the anchor heuristic and re-run; final CI status is PASS.

Risk and rollout: default behavior remains backward-compatible (regex mode unchanged) for existing customers. The new safe-fallback mode is enabled by default for hosted streaming routes that have toolcall=true to mitigate customer impact; Dedicated instances can toggle via their config. We also added an opt-out header (X-Redwood-Constraint-Mode: strict) to maintain compatibility for customers who rely on strict regex behavior.

Related: ENG-3421 (structured-output regressions), SUP-1287 (customer incident), ENG-3499 (streaming reframe RFC).

Notes for reviewers: focus on tokenizer/aligner correctness and the heuristics in proxy/fallback.go; look for edgecases around multibyte UTF-8 boundaries and recursive CFG anchor generation. The fallback synthesizer intentionally errs on the side of permissiveness to avoid false positives that drop tokens.
commits: a1b3f6a: tokenizer: add span aligner and confidence scoring (tokenizer/aligner.go)
b4c2d9e: constraints: introduce regex->CFG fallback proxy and config hooks (constraints/proxy.go)
c5d7f01: streaming: buffer partial tokens and add re-emit markers for resumed chunks (stream/chunker.go)
d8e2a9b: compat: fix function-call framing edgecases and add OpenAI-compat tests (compat/openai_toolcall_test.go)
review_comments: Ethan Park: Nice isolation between tokenizer and constraints. One concern: aligner confidence thresholds are currently hard-coded; can we make them configurable and document the expected trade-offs?
Priya Nair: Responded: added constraints.streaming_confidence_threshold and documented defaults in docs/constraints.md. Kept conservative defaults used in CI benchmarks.

Luca Moretti: Found a UTF-8 boundary case in chunker.go where a 3-byte char split across chunks could be misclassified as partial token - see inline. Suggest adding a regression to cover emoji sequences.
Priya Nair: Responded: fixed boundary detection and added test case for emoji-surrogate patterns in openai_toolcall_test.go.
Zoe Chen: Ran perf microbenchmarks; median latency impact is +1.8% in our standard throughput test, within acceptable bounds. Approving pending small nits on comments.
merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2024-06-10 after approvals from reviewers. No post-merge hotfixes required. Release notes added to CHANGELOG.md under 'Structured output / streaming'.
release_notes: Adds tokenizer-aware token-span alignment and a regex->CFG safe-fallback proxy to stabilize streaming function-call framing and constrained decoding across subtoken boundaries. Default behavior remains compatible; new safe-fallback mode reduces malformed toolcall regressions in streaming. See docs/constraints.md for migration and tuning guidance.
post_merge_actions: Deployed feature toggle to hosted streaming routes (constraints.streaming_mode = safe-fallback)
Notified SRE and Customer Success of SUP-1287 mitigation
Added regression to weekly CI smoke-suite
